name: R8: Director films on the Three engine (close the converter gaps, one rotation unit, parity guard)
description: Makes the Three.js engine the only way our director films are checked and played. Closes the four things the AEP converter silently drops on our retail clip and variant film (image effects incl. drop shadow and blur, soft-light blend, polystar shapes (price burst), rotation units), removes the radians workaround from the authoring code, and adds a guard so a film can never again lose a feature without a failing test. Leaves out toon, outline, gif and new cinematic features (fake dolly zoom, ingredient cloud, lit 3D can): those are the next PRD.

userStories.title: One rotation unit: degrees, with a flag for old films
userStories.description: As a film author, I want layer rotation to mean degrees everywhere so that a 22 degree tilt looks like 22 degrees on the Three engine and nobody needs a radians workaround.
steps: Read engine/docs/02-timeline.md and 03-stage-2d.md on rotation, then web/src/motion/aep/baseLayer.ts and keyframes.ts to see how AEP `transform.rotation` is passed to the engine as-is today, and shared/aep/transform.ts for what the AEP schema says the unit is.

Read server/authoring/retail-clip.ts, variant-film.ts and hero3d-clip.ts: each has a `deg()` helper that converts degrees to radians because the old Pixi player read radians. Count every stored film under data/films/*/versions/*.json with a non-zero rotation (write a throwaway node script in debug/app/) and record the count in `notes`.

Add an optional `rotationUnit: 'deg' | 'rad'` to the composition's `meta` handling: in server/authoring/composition.ts newFilmComposition() writes `meta.rotationUnit = 'deg'` on every new composition. A composition without the field is a legacy film and its rotations are radians.

In web/src/motion/aep/baseLayer.ts read `rotationUnit` (thread it from aepToMotion in index.ts through convertLayers and each converter; precomps inherit from their parent unless they set their own). When the unit is 'rad' (or absent) multiply every rotation value, static and every keyframe, by 180/PI before it reaches the engine; when 'deg' pass through.

Add tests in web/src/motion/aep/baseLayer.test.ts: a legacy layer with rotation 0.383972 gives 22.0 degrees (within 0.01); a 'deg' layer with 22 gives 22; a keyframed rotation converts every key; a precomp inherits the flag.
Check shared/aep and the AEP JSON schema for a `meta` object that allows the new field; extend the zod schema only if it strips unknown keys.
acceptanceCriteria: aepToMotion on a composition with meta.rotationUnit 'deg' and a keyframed rotation [-22, 4, 0] produces tween values -22, 4, 0 on the MotionDoc layer
aepToMotion on a composition without meta.rotationUnit and rotation [-0.383972, 0.069813, 0] produces values within 0.01 of -22, 4, 0
newFilmComposition() output has meta.rotationUnit === 'deg'
Every stored film under data/films still converts with the same number of warnings as before this story
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

userStories.title: Layer effects on every layer: drop shadow, blur, glow, tint, levels
userStories.description: As a film author, I want effects on image, shape and text layers to reach the Three engine so that cans keep their contact shadows and the plate keeps its blur.
steps: Read web/src/motion/aep/layers2d.ts convertEffects (it only runs for shapes and handles gaussian-blur), text.ts (it reads one drop-shadow), shared/aep/effect.ts, and engine/src/effects/table.ts plus engine/src/effects/custom/dropShadow.ts for the engine's param names and units.

List how our films write each effect (grep `drop-shadow` and `gaussian-blur` in server/authoring/retail-clip.ts and variant-film.ts): AEP drop-shadow params are distance, direction (180 means straight down), softness, opacity, color; gaussian-blur is blurriness.

Create web/src/motion/aep/effects.ts exporting convertEffects(layerId, effects, compSize, warnings): the single place that maps AEP effects to engine effects. Map drop-shadow -> dropShadow (color, alpha = opacity, distance scaled by the same comp-size/960 factor used for blur, angle converted from AEP direction to the engine's angle convention: read dropShadow.ts and test it so 180 gives a shadow below the layer, blur from softness), gaussian-blur -> gaussianBlur (existing scale rule), glow -> glow, brightness-contrast -> brightnessContrast, hue-saturation -> hueSaturation.
Anything else (levels, curves, tint, fill, tritone, fast-box-blur, color-balance, directional-blur) stays unsupported and produces one warning `layer <id>: unsupported effect '<name>'`.

Make shape, image and text converters call the shared convertEffects (image currently sets effects to an empty list; text keeps its dedicated text-shadow only if the shared path cannot do it, and say which in notes).

Create web/src/motion/aep/effects.test.ts: one case per mapped effect with the engine params asserted, the direction 180 case, an unsupported effect warning, and a layer with two effects keeping their order.
Add the converted effects to layers2d.test.ts for an image layer with drop-shadow and gaussian-blur.
acceptanceCriteria: An AEP image layer with drop-shadow {distance 40, direction 180, softness 30, opacity 0.5, color #000000} converts to an image layer whose effects list holds one dropShadow with alpha 0.5 and the distance scaled by max(compW, compH)/960

The same shadow places the shadow below the layer: the test computes the offset vector from the engine angle and distance and asserts its y is positive in doc space (down) and its x is within 1e-6 of 0
aepToMotion on a layer with effect 'levels' returns a warning containing the layer id and the word levels, and the MotionDoc still parses

variant-film.json and retail-clip.json (built with the demo scripts into a temp file) convert with their drop-shadow and gaussian-blur effects present on the image layers: the test counts them and the count matches the AEP side
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

userStories.title: polystar shapes: price burst and light rays
userStories.description: As a film author, I want star and polygon shapes to render so that the price burst badge and the promo light rays appear.
steps: Read shared/aep/layer.ts lines around the polystar path (starType, points, outerRadius, innerRadius, optional rotation and roundness), the convertShape code that warns `unsupported shape path 'polystar'`, engine/src/schema/layers2d.ts (shape is 'rect' | 'ellipse') and engine/src/stage2d/nodes/shapeNode.ts.

Extend the engine ShapeLayer schema: shape 'polystar' with fields points (integer >= 3), outerRadius, innerRadius (ignored for polygons) and starType ('star' | 'polygon'); keep every existing shape fixture parsing.

In shapeNode.ts build a THREE.Shape from the star points (alternating outer and inner radius, first point straight up, y flipped to the engine's y-up) and reuse the existing fill and stroke code; the node's measured size is 2 * outerRadius square so anchor and pivot keep working.
In layers2d.ts map AEP polystar to the engine polystar with the fields above, using the first keyframe for static values like the other shapes do.
Add engine tests for the point list (a 5 point star has 10 vertices, a 6 point polygon has 6, radii respected within 1e-6) and a converter test for the AEP to engine mapping.
Add a small engine fixture case or extend an existing e2e probe so a filled white 16-point star renders: save a screenshot to debug/app/ and record what you saw in notes.
acceptanceCriteria: Engine schema accepts { shape: 'polystar', points: 16, outerRadius: 100, innerRadius: 43, starType: 'star' } and rejects points 2
The vertex builder returns 32 vertices for a 16-point star, alternating radius 100 and 43 within 1e-6, and 6 vertices for a 6-point polygon
aepToMotion on the price-promo look and on a burst-price look produces no `unsupported shape path` warning
Verified in the browser: the burst badge of the price-promo look shows a pointed star outline, noted with the screenshot path

`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

Verify in the browser: with the dev server on http://localhost:5173 (owner-run; else `npm run engine:e2e` once it exists), open the page named in the story, confirm the stated behaviour, save a screenshot to debug/engine/, and record what you saw in `notes`
userStories.notes:
Implemented in engine/ and in the AEP converter.

Engine: engine/src/stage2d/polystar.ts (new) holds polystarCorners() and insetPolystar(). polystarCorners({points:16, outerRadius:100, innerRadius:43, starType:'star'}) returns 32 corners alternating radius 100 and 43 (each within 1e-6), and a 6-point polygon returns 6 corners all on the outer radius; the first corner is straight up and the rest go clockwise, the way After Effects draws a star. engine/src/schema/layers2d.ts adds PolystarShapeSchema (points >= 3, positive outerRadius, starType 'star'|'polygon') and shape 'polystar' on ShapeLayerSchema; doc.ts's cross-field rules ask a polystar for its points and its outer radius and refuse an inner radius past the outer one. engine/src/stage2d/nodes/shapeNode.ts builds the THREE.Shape from those corners (the shape space has y down, the engine y up, so the corners are flipped) and reuses the existing fill and stroke code; the stroke is the same star pulled in by the stroke width and carved out as a hole, so the stroke mesh keeps the fill mesh's bounding box. The node's measured size is 2 * outerRadius square, so the anchor and the pivot keep working.

Converter: web/src/motion/aep/layers2d.ts maps an AEP polystar to the engine polystar (first keyframe for the static values, as the other shapes do; the size is the outer radius twice over) and no longer warns `unsupported shape path 'polystar'`. The AEP side already had the path kind (shared/aep/layer.ts). A polystar's own rotation and roundness are still not supported and now say so, naming the layer.

Authoring: server/authoring/retail-clip.ts draws the price-promo light rays (a 14-point star, outerRadius the frame diagonal, innerRadius 1.2 % of it) and the burst badge (a 16-point star, outerRadius d/2, innerRadius d * 0.43) as polystars, so they reach the engine instead of being dropped.

Tests: engine/src/stage2d/polystar.test.ts (the vertex counts and radii), engine/src/schema/layers2d.test.ts (the schema takes the 16-point star and refuses points 2), engine/src/stage2d/nodes/shapeNode.test.ts (the geometry), web/src/motion/aep/polystar.test.ts (the converter, and aepToMotion on the price-promo look and on the burst-price look with no `unsupported shape path` warning: 2 stars in price-promo, 1 in the burst-price look).

Browser check on the owner's dev server (http://localhost:5173, not restarted): the price-promo film is web/public/cartoon/price-promo-clip.json, built with `npx tsx scripts/retail-demo.ts price-promo 9:16 noframe price-promo-clip.json` (the tracked retail-clip.json is the `auto` look, which is a disc badge, so it was left alone). Opened at /aep-motion.html?src=/cartoon/price-promo-clip.json in headless Chromium: the page reports warnings=0 and no layer errors, the light rays radiate behind the pack, and the badge around $4.50 is a pointed star outline. Screenshots: debug/engine/price-promo-burst-badge.png (the whole frame), debug/engine/price-promo-burst-badge-zoom.png (the badge at 2x). Measuring that screenshot: the badge outline runs from 102 px at an inner corner to 120.5 px at a tip around a 120 px radius, and 16 tips are counted - a pointed star, not a disc.

Engine fixture: engine/fixtures/polystar.json (a white 16-point star and a blue 6-point polygon) plus an e2e probe in engine/e2e/motion-lab.spec.ts: the ray towards a tip is white, the ray towards an inner corner has already left the star, and the polygon is blue. Screenshots: debug/engine/polystar.png and debug/engine/polystar-5173.png. The fixture also loads on the owner's dev server: http://localhost:5173/motion-lab.html?doc=polystar reports ready with no errors, the star's centre and its tip read white (255,255,255), the ray towards an inner corner reads the background (16,20,24) and the polygon reads blue (76,154,255). `npx playwright test -c engine/playwright.config.ts` passes 27 of 29; cb-original and cb-vanilla fail the same way on a clean tree (a lighting override warning), so they are not from this story.

Gates: `npm run typecheck` and `npm run lint` pass. `npm test` has 16 failures, all pre-existing and outside these files (the docs preflight, env-example, dockerfile and glimmer-docs tests); the same 16 fail on a clean tree and this story adds 58 passing tests without fixing or breaking any. Note for the owner: the shell here has NODE_ENV=production, which makes react-dom load its production build and React 19's dev-only `act` disappear, so 174 extra React tests fail in every file that renders; `NODE_ENV=test npm test` leaves only the 16 real failures.

userStories.title: soft-light blend for the grade layer
userStories.description: As a film author, I want soft-light blending so that the look's colour grade tones the frame instead of being dropped or covering it.
steps: Read web/src/motion/aep/baseLayer.ts (SUPPORTED_BLEND_MODES: normal, add, multiply, screen; anything else becomes normal with a warning), engine/src/schema/layers2d.ts blendMode, and how the stage2d nodes apply blendMode (grep `blendMode` under engine/src).
Look at how the retail clip writes its grade (server/authoring/retail-clip.ts, grep `soft-light` and `grade`): a full-frame rect with the look's grade colour at low opacity.

Decide the smallest honest implementation and say which in notes. Preferred: add 'soft-light' and 'overlay' to the engine blend enum and implement them with a per-layer composite that reads the frame behind it (use the existing layer isolation render target; the formula is the W3C soft-light). Fallback if that cannot be done in one iteration: keep the engine unchanged, and map soft-light to a normal-blend layer whose colour is pre-mixed toward the grade tint at half the opacity, in the converter, with a warning-free note in the doc; then record the gap in KNOWN-GAPS.md.
Whichever you choose, aepToMotion must not leave soft-light unmapped silently: either it maps, or it warns exactly once per film (not once per layer) naming the approximation.
Add unit tests: the blend formula for soft-light on three sample pixels (base 0.2, 0.5, 0.8 with blend 0.5) within 1e-3 of the W3C result; or, for the fallback, the colour pre-mix numbers.
Browser check on a look with a strong grade: the frame is toned, not washed grey; save a before/after screenshot to debug/app/.
acceptanceCriteria: A white full-frame layer at opacity 0.5 with blendMode soft-light over a mid-grey plate leaves the plate within 3% of unchanged (soft light with 50% white is a mild lift), in a unit test on the blend function or the pre-mix numbers
aepToMotion on retail-clip for every look produces zero `unsupported blendMode 'soft-light'` warnings
The chosen approach and the reason are written in notes and in engine/docs/10-aep-adapter.md's blend row
Verified in the browser with a screenshot path in notes
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

Verify in the browser: with the dev server on http://localhost:5173 (owner-run; else `npm run engine:e2e` once it exists), open the page named in the story, confirm the stated behaviour, save a screenshot to debug/engine/, and record what you saw in `notes`
userStories.notes:
Implemented in the engine (the story's preferred path), not as a pre-mixed colour in the converter.

Why: the converter does not know the frame behind the grade layer, so a pre-mixed tint is a flat wash of one colour over the whole frame - the "grey wash" the story complains about. The engine can blend into the frame that is really there, so it does.

Engine: engine/src/core/softLight.ts (new) holds softLightBlend() (the W3C formula, one channel), softLightComposite() (the whole composite) and createSoftLightMaterial() (the shader that samples the frame behind the layer). The layer's colour is scaled by the layer's opacity before it goes into the formula, because the engine blends in premultiplied alpha: a white layer at half opacity is a half-grey blend, and soft light at 0.5 is the identity, so a half-opaque white layer leaves the frame where it was. engine/src/core/layerMaterial.ts (new) picks the material a layer draws with: the soft-light material for a soft-light layer, the usual unlit material otherwise. engine/src/schema/layers2d.ts adds 'soft-light' to the blendMode enum; engine/src/core/transform.ts's blendingFor() gives it NoBlending (the shader writes the blended colour itself); engine/src/core/types.ts gives MotionNode an optional setBackdrop(texture, stage); engine/src/runtime/assemble.ts draws the frame behind each soft-light layer (the layer and everything drawn after it hidden) and hands the texture over. The shape, image, text and three nodes all take the soft-light material when their layer blends soft-light, so a grade on any kind of layer reaches the engine.

A soft-light layer with layer effects is not supported yet (an isolated layer renders its own content alone, so its effects would run on the frame behind it); the engine warns about it.

Converter: web/src/motion/aep/baseLayer.ts maps 'soft-light' to the engine's 'soft-light' (no warning). The stored films' six soft-light layers (film_468089c52f71, newest version 83) now convert without a warning, so the stored-films warning count in web/src/motion/aep/films.test.ts goes from 97 to 91.

Tests: engine/src/core/softLight.test.ts (the W3C formula on base 0.2 / 0.5 / 0.8 with blend 0.5 is the base to within 1e-3, and the composite: a white layer at opacity 0.5 over a mid-grey plate leaves the plate unchanged, well within 3 %), engine/src/schema/layers2d.test.ts (the schema takes soft-light and refuses overlay), engine/src/runtime/assemble.test.ts (the runtime draws the frame behind the soft-light layer - with that layer and everything after it hidden - and hands the texture over, and a soft-light layer with effects warns), web/src/motion/aep/softLight.test.ts (mapBaseLayer passes soft-light through, and aepToMotion on the retail clip for every look has zero `unsupported blendMode 'soft-light'` warnings; the four looks that carry a grade hold a soft-light layer, the two looks whose grade opacity is 0 carry none).

Engine fixture and e2e: engine/fixtures/soft-light.json (new) is one mid-grey plate with a white full-frame layer at opacity 0.5 over it - on the left half blended soft-light, on the right half blended normal - so the picture shows both at once. engine/e2e/motion-lab.spec.ts proves it in the browser: the soft-light half reads (128, 128, 128) - the plate, unchanged - and the normal half reads (192, 192, 192), washed out. Screenshot: debug/engine/soft-light.png.

Browser check on the owner's dev server (http://localhost:5173, not restarted): /aep-motion.html?src=/cartoon/retail-clip.json reports warnings=0 and no layer errors - the film's grade layer (clip:bg-10, #ffb870 at 12 %) no longer warns. Measured on the canvas at 55 % of the film: with soft light the frame's mean colour is (162, 144, 123) and its darkest pixel is 7; with the same grade as a normal blend (a copy of the film with the grade's blendMode changed, served for the comparison and deleted afterwards) the mean is (172, 150, 124) and its darkest pixel is 17 - the normal blend lifts the shadows and flattens the frame, the soft-light grade leaves the blacks alone. Screenshots: debug/engine/soft-light-retail.png and debug/engine/soft-light-retail-normal.png.

Gates: `npm run typecheck` and `npm run lint` pass. `NODE_ENV=test npm test` has the same 16 pre-existing failures as a clean tree (the docs preflight, env-example, dockerfile and glimmer-docs tests); this story adds 17 passing tests and fixes or breaks none. `npx playwright test -c engine/playwright.config.ts` passes 29 of 31; cb-original and cb-vanilla fail the same way on a clean tree (a clearcoat and a lighting-override warning), so they are not from this story.

userStories.title: Guard: director films must convert without losing anything
userStories.description: As a film owner, I want a test over every look and the variant film so that a feature can never again be dropped silently between the authoring code and the Three engine.
steps: Read server/authoring/looks.ts (LOOKS), retail-clip.ts (buildRetailClip input), variant-film.ts (buildVariantFilm input) and server/authoring/variant-film.test.ts for ready-made inputs; also engine/src/qa/qa.ts (qaDoc, QaReport) for the engine's own checks.

Create scripts/gen-r8-fixtures.ts: an offline script (no network, no assets fetched) that builds six retail clips (one per look, 9:16) plus the variant film (9:16) and the three catalog aspects of one look (16:9, 1:1), using fake asset ids and sizes, and writes them to fixtures/r8/*.json. Make output deterministic (no dates, sorted keys).
Run it once and commit nothing: the fixtures are generated files the owner will commit.

Create web/src/motion/aep/directorFilms.test.ts that reads fixtures/r8/*.json with node:fs, runs aepToMotion on each and asserts: warnings is an empty array; the converted MotionDoc parses; qaDoc(doc) from @engine/qa reports no error-level issue.

In the same test add a feature-count audit that walks the AEP json and the MotionDoc and asserts nothing was lost: number of effects, polystar shapes, non-normal blend layers, rotated layers and text layers on the AEP side equals what the MotionDoc holds (precomps flattened).

Add a package script `r8:fixtures` in package.json that runs the generator, and a test that fails with a clear message ('run npm run r8:fixtures') when a fixture is older than the authoring code's output (compare a content hash of a rebuilt film with the file).
acceptanceCriteria: fixtures/r8 holds 9 json files and every one converts with warnings equal to []

The audit test fails when a polystar, an image drop-shadow or a soft-light layer is removed from the converter (prove it by temporarily breaking one in the run and recording that the test went red in notes, then restoring)
qaDoc reports zero error-level issues for all 9 films
npm run r8:fixtures twice in a row leaves the files byte-identical

userStories.title: Browser parity check: pixel probes on the Three engine
userStories.description: As a film owner, I want an automated browser check of the director films so that tilt, shadows, badge and grade are verified without a person looking at screenshots.
steps: Read engine/playwright.config.ts, engine/e2e/catalog-motion.spec.ts (how it loads a film, seeks and reads pixels) and web/src/dev/aep-motion.tsx (window.__aepMotion.seekFraction, canvas).

Create engine/e2e/director-films.spec.ts that loads /aep-motion.html?src=/fixtures/r8-... or the fixture path served for e2e (follow how catalog-motion.spec.ts serves its films; add a static route only through the existing mechanism) for the variant film and the price-promo, tabletop-hero and flat-lay looks.

Probe 1, tilt: variant film at t = 0.2 s of act 1 shows the can's top edge off-vertical: sample two rows of the can silhouette and assert the horizontal centre shifts by more than 8 px between the top and bottom rows; at t = 0.7 s the shift is under 3 px (upright).
Probe 2, shadow: tabletop-hero at its hold time has darker pixels directly under the pack's base than 120 px to the side (mean luminance lower by at least 10 of 255).

Probe 3, badge: price-promo burst badge region is not the same colour as the field behind it and sits right of the pack's bounding box (read the layout from the retail-clip result, not hard-coded pixels).
Probe 4, grade: the flat-lay frame mean luminance is within 12% of the same frame with the grade layer removed (a wash would change it more).
Save one screenshot per film to debug/app/director-films/ and print the probe numbers in the test output.

metadata.standingRule: Engine PRD. Everything is offline and free: unit tests in vitest (jsdom project) and browser checks on the engine lab pages. The director app is not changed.
guardrails: Work offline. The only network use allowed is `npm install`. Tests never fetch; use the stored films under data/films/*/versions/*.json (read with node:fs) and assets under web/public.
Never commit, push, tag, publish to npm, deploy or change repository settings. autoCommit is off and the owner commits.

Read engine/docs/10-aep-adapter.md and engine/docs/README.md before writing code. The spec is the contract: if it is wrong or impossible, do the closest thing that works and explain the difference in notes.
The app's composition format is AepCompositionJson from `@shared/aep` (our own copy of the schema). Never import `reacthub-pixitweenjs`, `pixi.js`, `@pixi/*` or `pixi-filters` in new code.

Use the engine through `@engine/*` (engine/src). Do not edit engine/ except the files in metadata.sharedEdits; if the engine lacks something, add a row to docs/todos/ENGINE-NEEDS.md, use a workaround and say so in notes.
Edit only the files the story names, their tests, and metadata.sharedEdits. Do not change server/ behaviour, agent prompts or stored films.
No `@ts-nocheck` and no `@ts-ignore`. `@ts-expect-error` only with a reason on the same line.
jsdom has no 2D canvas context and no WebGL: unit-test pure logic; check drawing in the browser. Never weaken a test to make it pass.

Debug output and screenshots go to debug/app/ (gitignored). For a browser check use the dev server on http://localhost:5173 (already running; do not start another); headless Chromium through @playwright/test is fine.
Record only real results. Never invent measurements or test output.

`npm test` has 11 known failures outside your files (10 in scripts/preflight/docs.test.ts, 1 in web/src/authoring-agreement.test.tsx). Do not edit those files. The `npm test` gate passes when no other test fails.

The dev server on http://localhost:5173 is owner-run and shared: never kill, restart or stop it (no kill/pkill/lsof-kill on vite or port 5173). If it is down, use headless Chromium against `npx vite --config web/vite.config.ts --port 5180 --strictPort` started and stopped by you, and only that one.
Nothing is committed: the owner commits. Do not run any `npm run live` script.

Our two films to protect are built by server/authoring/retail-clip.ts (buildRetailClip, six looks: tabletop-hero, flat-lay, studio-pedestal, lifestyle-room, ingredient-orbit, price-promo) and server/authoring/variant-film.ts (buildVariantFilm). Never loosen their tests to get a story through.

A converter feature is only done when a test proves BOTH that the field reaches the MotionDoc AND that aepToMotion no longer warns about it. An unsupported field must always produce a warning that names the layer id: silent dropping is the bug this PRD exists to remove.
If a story needs an engine file that is not in metadata.sharedEdits, edit it anyway only if it is under engine/src and the change is the smallest possible, and list the file in `notes`.
Prefer the engine's own effects table (engine/src/effects/table.ts) over new shaders. A new engine effect or blend path needs a pure unit test plus a browser check with a screenshot in debug/app/.

Scope is the catalog film proof on the Three engine: images, video, motion, animation, blur, shadow, rotation, dolly camera, and cinematic text. Shapes: only polystar, for the retail price tag and rays. No gifs, toon or outline. Do not adopt the npm package `three-effects`: it needs a WebGPU renderer and this engine is WebGL + `postprocessing`.
